transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, I came in because... well, I drive a cab, and even when I know for a fact I did my safety check on the car, this thought just keeps hitting me that I missed something. 

I keep thinking that because I messed up, somebody could get hurt, or my boss is gonna say I lied about doing the check in the first place. It's just... I can't make the thought shut up. It's in my head the whole time I'm driving, or even when I'm just trying to sit down and study. It's really getting to be too much.
When you get these thoughts about missing the safety check, do you find yourself going back to double-check the car, or doing anything else repeatedly to try to make the thought go away?

Yeah, I do. Um, before I can even take a ride, I just... I keep going around the car. I check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, all my paperwork. And I do it over and over. 

Sometimes I even take pictures of everything on my phone, and if something just doesn't feel right, I have to restart the whole check from the very beginning. I end up doing this even when I have passengers standing there waiting for me and I'm already late. I just have to do it.

latest_inference.note: Patient demonstrates clear obsessions (intrusive thoughts about missed safety checks) and compulsions (repetitive checking rituals, taking pictures, restarting checks). This is pathognomonic for OCD (F42). Generalized anxiety (F41.1, F41.0) and other neurotic disorders (F48.8) are ruled out as primary diagnoses given the specific obsessive-compulsive pattern with functional impairment.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation shows intrusive thoughts about safety checks and catastrophic consequences, persistent worry despite reassurance, and functional impairment. This suggests obsessive-compulsive disorder as primary candidate, with generalized anxiety disorder and specific phobia as differentials. F48.8 included for other specified neurotic disorders pending clarification.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with classic obsessive-compulsive disorder characterized by intrusive obsessions (repeated thoughts about missing safety checks despite knowing they were completed) and compulsive behaviors (repetitive checking of car, taking pictures, restarting checks). The obsessions cause significant distress, the compulsions are performed to reduce anxiety, and there is clear functional impairment (tardiness, inability to focus on studying, interference with work duties).

Fear that boss will accuse patient of lying about completing safety check

Obsessions present during driving and while attempting to study
Repetitive checking of car components (tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork)
Multiple rounds of checking performed sequentially
Taking pictures of all checked items on phone
Restarting entire checking sequence if something 'doesn't feel right'
Compulsions performed despite external pressure (waiting passengers, being late for rides)
Tardiness arriving to pick up passengers
Interference with work duties and passenger service
Recognition that compulsions are excessive and problematic

additional_requirements: Obsessions recognized as intrusive and distressing
